Face: Which emotion does the face show?
Face. The board has 10x10 sites (160x160 cells). The window shows one site; each move goes to the next site (up, down, left or right). One large face fills the board. Two brows sit at the top, two eyes below them, the two mouth corners lower down and the middle of the mouth at the bottom; every other site shows plain skin. The whole face may sit up to one site higher, lower, left or right. Question: Which emotion does the face show? The answer is one of eight emotions, each with its own brows, eyes and mouth: happy = lowered brows, open eyes, mouth corners up, a closed mouth; sad = raised brows, open eyes, mouth corners down, a closed mouth; angry = lowered brows, open eyes, mouth corners down, an open mouth; surprised = raised brows, open eyes, mouth corners up, an open mouth; sleepy = lowered brows, closed eyes, mouth corners down, a closed mouth; scared = raised brows, closed eyes, mouth corners down, an open mouth; calm = raised brows, closed eyes, mouth corners up, a closed mouth; laughing = lowered brows, closed eyes, mouth corners up, an open mouth. Answer with its name. You may answer at any time; you do not need to see every site. Score: 20 if the answer is right, minus 10, minus 0.1 per move (movement budget 35).
The answers: 1 = happy, 2 = sad, 3 = angry, 4 = surprised, 5 = sleepy, 6 = scared, 7 = calm, 8 = laughing.
You see the board, 10 x 10 sites, only through a window of one site (16 x 16 cells). A move goes to the next site. At most 35 moves.
